title: Exos API
description: A read-only REST API over one organization's Exos data: events, ticket types, attendees, door scans, orders, invoices, refunds and webhooks. Use it to sync sales into a CRM or a spreadsheet, show your events on your own site, or build reports. Every request is scoped to the organization of the API key that makes it; nothing in the API changes data. Requests are GET, responses are JSON, and times are ISO 8601 strings in UTC. Paths below are relative to the base URL (the exos-api edge function of your Supabase project), e.g. https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/functions/v1/exos-api/v1/events. Each path also answers without the /v1 prefix, for clients of the first release. Call the API from your server: it sends no CORS headers, and a key in a browser is a key anyone can copy.

authentication.description: Send an organization API key as a bearer token. An owner or manager creates keys in Org settings → Developer, choosing the scopes each key gets; the key (sk_live_ plus 48 hex characters) is shown once, and only its SHA-256 hash and a 16-character prefix are stored. An organization has at most 10 active keys. Keys do not expire: they work until revoked, and a key is revoked automatically when the member who created it leaves the organization. A request for anything outside the key's organization answers 404, so ids from other organizations cannot be probed.
authentication.token_validity: API keys do not expire; revoke one in Org settings when it is no longer needed.

methods.name: Organization API key
methods.description: Every endpoint. Held to the scopes chosen when the key was created (an owner or manager can change them later). Keys created before scopes existed carry the legacy `read` scope, which covers every `:read` scope.

authentication.scopes_description: Every endpoint needs one scope, named on the endpoint; GET /v1/me needs none. A key without the scope gets 403 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope". A `:write` scope covers the `:read` scope of the same resource, and the legacy `read` scope covers every `:read` scope. Scopes for areas without routes yet (booking, finance) and the `:write` scopes can already be granted, so a key can be narrowed ahead of the routes that will use them. GET /v1/me returns a key's scopes as stored and as they take effect.

pagination.description: List endpoints marked as paged take page and per_page and answer { data, meta }. meta.total is the number of rows matching the filters and meta.total_pages the number of pages at this per_page; walk the list by asking for page + 1 until page >= total_pages. A page past the end answers an empty data array. Each list has a fixed order (documented per endpoint) with a tiebreak on the id, so pages do not overlap while the data is unchanged. Endpoints that are not paged answer { data: [...] } with every row. A bad page or per_page answers 400.

rate_limiting.description: 120 requests per API key per clock minute (a fixed one-minute window), counted for every authenticated request, errors included. Over the limit the answer is 429 { "error": "rate limit exceeded", "limit_per_minute": 120 } with a Retry-After header: the seconds until the next minute starts. If the rate limiter itself is unavailable the request is refused with 503 and Retry-After: 30, because the API returns personal data and is never served unmetered.

limits.limit: 120 requests a minute per API key

error_format.description: Errors are JSON with a human-readable error message. Some carry a little more: 403 names the scope that was needed, 429 the limit, and 404 for an unknown path a hint.

error_codes.name: Bad request
error_codes.description: A bad page, per_page or filter value; the message names it.

error_codes.name: Unauthorized
error_codes.description: No bearer key ("missing bearer API key"), or a key that is unknown or revoked ("invalid or revoked API key").

error_codes.name: Forbidden
error_codes.description: The key lacks the endpoint's scope. The body names it (required_scope) and so does the WWW-Authenticate header: Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="…".

error_codes.name: Not found
error_codes.description: An unknown path, or an event or order that does not exist in the key's organization.

error_codes.name: Method not allowed
error_codes.description: Anything but GET (the API is read-only). The Allow header says GET.

error_codes.name: Too many requests
error_codes.description: Over 120 requests this minute for this key; wait Retry-After seconds.

error_codes.name: Server error
error_codes.description: Unexpected; safe to retry, since every call is a read.

error_codes.name: Unavailable
error_codes.description: The rate limiter could not be reached, so the request was refused; retry after Retry-After seconds.

webhooks.description: Exos can also push: register an HTTPS endpoint in Org settings → Developer and it receives a signed POST for each event type it subscribes to (ticket.created, ticket.checked_in, order.fulfilled, order.refunded, event.published). GET /v1/webhooks lists the endpoints.

signature.format: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<X-Exos-Timestamp>.<raw body>" with the endpoint's secret>
signature.description: Compute the HMAC over the raw request body (before parsing the JSON), compare in constant time, and reject timestamps more than 5 minutes old. X-Exos-Delivery is the same on every retry of a delivery: dedupe on it.

headers.name: X-Exos-Delivery
headers.description: The delivery id; the same across retries.

headers.name: X-Exos-Timestamp
headers.description: Unix seconds when this attempt was sent.

webhooks.retries: A delivery that does not get a 2xx is retried with exponential backoff (about 2^attempt minutes, at most 6 hours apart); after 8 attempts it is given up. Redirects are not followed, and only https URLs at public addresses are called.
